newsitem.title: GERMANY: HypoBank sees good 1997 operating business.
newsitem.headline: HypoBank sees good 1997 operating business.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected continued good operating business in 1997, but said provisions for lending risks were likely to remain high.
Results in the first two months of the year had been "very satisfactory", chairman Eberhard Martini told a news conference.

The Bavarian bank reported a nine percent decline in operating profits after risk provisions for 1996, with a total of 1.19 billion marks after 1.304 billion the previous year. Net profits rose some six percent to 714.90 million marks.
In its annual report, also released today, the bank said it expected continued good operating business in 1997.
In 1996, its net interest income rose to 4.407.5 billion marks from 4,106.1 billion, while net commission income rose to 1,175.6 billion marks from 817.5 million.
However risk provisions, inflated by Germany's difficult economic conditions, surged to 1.315 billion marks from 833.30 million the previous year, eating into operating earnings.
HypoBank, a specialist in mortgage lending, said it saw little chance the need for high lending risk provisions would ease this year and expected provisions to remain at a high level.
Martini said operating profits after risk provisions had been in line with an "ambitious plan" in January 1997 and had exceeded the bank's goals in February.
